label: second input token after a leading z (specific token set)
explanation: Fires only at step t=1 (the second original token) in sequences whose first token is z, and only when that second token is one of a, c, y, w, b, l, v, f, d, s, q, 0. For those tokens it fires essentially every time; it never fires for other second tokens after z, in any other position, or in the delimiter/copy phases. Magnitude is set by the identity of the second token: a is highest (always about 1.0 of max), then c, s, f, d, v, q are mid-to-high, while y, w, b, 0, l are weak (0.08-0.22 of max). L has little effect.

issues: No refutation found. On the test split: precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0, mass recall about 1.0, 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

Dev profile supports every claim: all firing is at t=1 and in the original phase (delimiter and copy phases are 0). prev_tok=z and first_tok=z hold for 100% of activation mass. Only the 12 listed in_tok values appear.

The magnitude claims hold. Because t=1, the activation is set only by the token pair, so each second token has a constant value: a=1.00, f=0.66, d=0.58, v=0.42, y=0.22, w=0.19, b=0.15, 0=0.13, l=0.08. L-wise mass shares are flat (0.15 to 0.18 for L>=4), so L has little effect.
Small wording nit: 'a leading z' and 'prev_tok==z at t=1' mean the same thing, so the label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
